conclusions.statement: On coding benchmarks Sonnet 5.5 is not a cheap Opus 5.5: its token volume offsets its 50% token discount (Terminal-Bench 4.1: 22.22 USD per trial against 14.30, about twice the output tokens).

On interactive 3D scenes Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 at max are level within the 95% interval (AA-3D 1204 vs 1202), and Sonnet's derived cost per AA-3D task is about two thirds of Opus's. Fable 5.2 is ahead (1271).

On WebDev Arena (23 Nov) Opus 5.5 max is about 48 points above Sonnet 5.5 xhigh and about 105 above Sonnet 5.5 high, outside both intervals. The Arena 3D board shows the same order but a smaller gap for Sonnet high (Sonnet high does better on 3D than its overall level predicts).

Fleet agent runs are dominated by cached-input re-reads (gpt-6-sol high: 17.7 B cached-read tokens, about 74% of its list-price cost), so the per-token cache price is the main cost lever: gpt-6.1-sol (cached 0.10) dominates gpt-6-sol (cached 0.20) at the same input and output price.

Haiku 5.5 and Luna collapse at low and medium effort on hard reasoning (ARC-AGI-2: Haiku 2.8% / 9.4%, Luna 4.6% / 18.1%). They appear only in the mechanical (pure docs/config) and summary classes; the catalogue loader rejects a light-tier rung anywhere else.

AA-3D excludes scenes that do not run before the vote, so its Elo is preference among valid results and says nothing about how reliably a model produces something playable. Arena counts 'both bad' votes but publishes no per-model failure rate. Technical execution has to be measured on our own creative cards (playable rate).

benchmarks.judged: Interactive three.js scenes and small games built by an agent from a written brief (55 tasks, 7 domains, 3 h / 250 turns, offline sandbox with Blender, Rapier, headless browser and a CC0 asset library).
benchmarks.coverage: Max effort for Claude and OpenAI candidates; Gemini at high or xhigh. No Sonnet 5.5 high or Opus 5.5 low row.
benchmarks.notes: Panelists must view each scene at least 30 s and can interact with it; votes blind; Bradley-Terry with 95% sandwich intervals. Scenes must load within 60 s in a software-rendered headless browser, keep rendering, show a non-blank image and run offline, then pass a manual review. Cost per task is derived by TE-83 from AA's published token counts and prices (cache writes excluded).
gaps: No published share of excluded (non-running) scenes per model. TE-83 counted scenes in blind voting from AA's per-task coverage data on 54 of the 55 tasks: Fable 5.2 54, Opus 5.5 49, Sonnet 5.5 46, Haiku 5.5 50, GPT-6.1 Sol 52, GPT-6.2 Sol 54. This proxies valid-scene rate after AA's check; it is not a playable rate.
No rows below max effort for Claude or OpenAI models, so no ranking for Sonnet 5.5 high against Opus 5.5 low.
